breaking_changes: The version scheme changed from M.m.p to YYYY.WW.N format; CMake version extraction moved to a Python-based git state derivation system, MSI installer versions are reformatted as YY.MM.PATCH, and the get-version action now outputs YYYY.WW.N instead of the static CMake VERSION.

evidence.blockers: The candidate pipeline (658d565-2) is the only P0: it is a new shipping surface for release testing that has never been exercised end-to-end — without verifying MSI signing is skipped, candidate-v* tags are created, artifacts publish correctly, and release notes carry the unsigned-installer warning, we can't confidently build or test a release candidate. Downstream version-format handling (c47aa2a-3) is P1 — the YYYY>255 concern is real but the conversion code (YY.MM.PATCH) exists and needs verification, not a blocker.
evidence.breaking_changes: The version scheme is the primary breaking change. The YYYY.WW.N format with potential YYYY exceeding 255 affects MSI version fields, CMake variable derivation, and downstream packaging. The release-notes and announcement steps surface each entry from this list.
evidence.coverage: All 19 to-dos from the previous review have been rated. The digest contains 38 commits; 2 commits in this range have no commit review and are not in the digest.
evidence.manual_testing: Two user-facing new surfaces need human verification: the /v1/docs endpoint and the lemonade_docs MCP tool (both P1). The FLM ModelScope download path (P1) requires a macOS NPU-capable runner. HF API monitoring (6a60710-2, P1) should be tracked after the candidate ships to catch 429s from the extra compatibility-metadata call.
evidence.security: No new security concerns observed. The wildcard origin matching (6a5e307) has proper scheme enforcement. The GGUF architecture filter (6a60710) improves security by rejecting incompatible repositories. The MCP client revert (496bb24) reduces attack surface by removing an undocumented process-launch endpoint.

verdict_reason: One item still blocks the release: the candidate pipeline hasn't been verified end-to-end so we can't confidently test the release candidate. Downstream consumers need confirmation they handle the new version format, but that doesn't hold up the build itself. The rest of the list is P1 or P2 work that should be checked before shipping.
